     1	import dlt
     2	from pyspark.sql.functions import col, trim, regexp_replace, when, length, to_date
     3	from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
     4	
     5	spark = SparkSession.getActiveSession()
     6	catalog = spark.conf.get("catalog")
     7	target_schema = spark.conf.get("target_schema")  # silver target schema, e.g., consumer_silver
     8	# Derive bronze schema from silver target
     9	bronze_schema = target_schema.replace("_silver", "_bronze")
    10	bronze_table = f"{catalog}.{bronze_schema}.consumer_mv"
    11	
    12	@dlt.expect_or_drop("valid_consumer_id", "consumer_id IS NOT NULL")
    13	@dlt.table(
    14	    name="consumer_mv",
    15	    comment="Silver consumer view with cleaned data",
    16	    table_properties={"quality": "silver"}
    17	)
    18	def consumer_mv():
    19	    # Read from bronze view as a streaming source
    20	    df = spark.readStream.table(bronze_table)
    21	    # Trim whitespace from string columns
    22	    string_cols = ["name", "gender", "email", "phone", "address", "city", "state", "country"]
    23	    for c in string_cols:
    24	        df = df.withColumn(c, trim(col(c)))
    25	    # Phone: keep digits only
    26	    df = df.withColumn("phone", regexp_replace(col("phone"), r"\D", ""))
    27	    # Nullify phone if less than 10 digits
    28	    df = df.withColumn("phone", when(length(col("phone")) < 10, None).otherwise(col("phone")))
    29	    # Convert registration_date to date type
    30	    df = df.withColumn("registration_date", to_date(col("registration_date"), "yyyy-MM-dd"))
    31	    return df
